Two hands,
one bench,
no rush.

Hollow & Grain is a one-bench workshop on the north end of Bellingham, a few blocks from the bay. We make kitchen pieces the slow way — by hand, one at a time — because that's the only way that ever felt right.

We're not trying to be big. We're trying to make the board you'll still be using in thirty years.

The Long Version

How it started

It started with a leftover walnut slab and a borrowed hand plane in a one-car garage. The first board was for our own kitchen — too thick, slightly crooked, and we still use it every day. Friends asked for one. Then friends of friends. Eight years later the garage has become a proper shop, but not much else has changed.

We still pick every board off the lumber rack ourselves, matching grain by eye. We still glue up by hand, flatten with planes, and sand through five grits until the surface feels like skin. Every piece gets a coat of our own mineral-oil-and-beeswax finish before it leaves the bench, and a small branded stamp on the underside.

We're a catalog-and-inquiry shop, not a checkout cart. We'd rather have a quick conversation, get the details right, and make you exactly the thing you need — than sell you something off a shelf that's almost right.

Made by hand, on purpose

No CNC, no production line. The marks of the tools are part of the piece. If you want perfectly identical, machined boards, we're honestly not your shop.

Wood with a backstory

We buy from regional mills and small private timberlands across the Pacific Northwest. We know where most of our walnut and maple grew.

Built to be repaired

A board from us can be re-sanded, re-oiled, and brought back to life for decades. Send yours back anytime for a refresh — we only charge shipping.

Honest about timing

If we can't make your deadline, we'll tell you before you pay. A two-bench shop has limits, and we'd rather keep your trust than overpromise.
